name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah was a male Levite known as the son of Jehoiada the priest. His life is marked by a tragic end, as he was stoned to death in the court of the house of the Lord. This event underscores his significant role within the temple and the religious community of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means 'YHWH remembers,' reflecting a proper Hebrew name given not by God but recorded in Scripture. This name highlights the faithfulness of God in remembering His people, which is fitting for a priestly figure.
familyAndRelationships: Zechariah is explicitly identified as the son of Jehoiada, the priest. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance lies in his priestly lineage and his martyrdom within the temple precincts, illustrating the cost of faithfulness in a time of spiritual decline. His death by stoning in the house of the Lord serves as a solemn reminder of the consequences of opposing God's covenant community. Through his story, the biblical narrative emphasizes the importance of obedience and the dangers of forsaking God's commands.
